review: Independent adversarial review: goal decomposition graph, terminal read-failure shortcut, automatic completion path
reviewer: the reviewing agent (independent), not the author of the code under review
target: aries/workspace/agent.py (completion(), the decision.action == 'finish' branch, the terminal-failure call site)
aries/workspace/finish_proposal.py (read because it is the only producer of automatic finish decisions)

supporting surfaces read to judge the above: aries/workspace/contracts.py, aries/workspace/scopes.py, aries/workspace/registry.py, aries/workspace/orchestration.py (claim/roll_up/tick), aries/workspace/service.py (ACTIVE/cancel/dispatch/_supervise), aries/intelligence/budgets.py, aries/flags.py
method: Two kinds of evidence, labelled per finding and never mixed. (1) SOURCE INSPECTION: full reads of the four target files and of every function they depend on for their safety claims. (2) EXECUTED PROOF: five scripts run in-process against an isolated database (DATABASE_URL=sqlite+aiosqlite:////tmp/claude-review-*.db, PYTHONPATH=vendor/agentic-core:vendor:repo, interpreter .venv/bin/python). No service, no model call, no model-backed planner, nothing written to var/aries.db, and the project test suite was NOT run. The executed scripts: (p1) flag defaults, contracts.compile_goal over six goals, terminal_failure.reason over eight adversarial variants, verify_probe with a contradictory fresh probe; (p2) goal_graph.validate over eight adversarial plans plus scopes.enforce/scopes.use/expiry against the grants it produced; (p3) agent.completion over seven cases on real temp files created under /tmp (honest finish, invented ref, unverified-observation ref, empty refs, file changed underneath, file deleted, unverified step) plus verify_exists on a missing path (with capabilities.checked_path stubbed to an identity function, because that call needs settings this harness does not create) and contracts.answer for a bare system.status contract; (p4) goal_graph.dependencies_ready against real WorkspaceGoal rows with a cancelled parent; (p5) goal_graph.validate plus agent.completion on a reversed-node-order decomposition, reproducing synthesize()'s exact call shape. Temp files were created only under /tmp and the system temp dir; no file under aries/, eval/ or experiments/ was modified except this output file.
configuration_note: ARIES_GOAL_TEAMS defaults to FALSE (aries/flags.py:58, confirmed by executed proof: no var/flags.env exists, so defaults apply). Every goal_graph finding below is therefore latent in the default configuration and reachable only with the flag on. ARIES_TERMINAL_READ_FAILURE, ARIES_CONTRACT_FINISH and ARIES_COMPLETION_PROGRESS_GUARD all default to TRUE and are live.

findings.title: A queued child can be admitted to run after its parent has been cancelled; claim() never checks the parent's state
findings.observed: EXECUTED PROOF: with a parent WorkspaceGoal row in state 'cancelled', goal_graph.dependencies_ready returned (True, None) both for a child whose prerequisite had reached 'done' with final_evidence_refs and for a child with no declared dependencies. SOURCE INSPECTION: orchestration.claim gates a launch on exactly four things - orchestration.role == 'child', dependencies_ready (which reads only data['orchestration']['depends_on']), resource admission, and a compare-and-swap on the child's own row from 'queued' to 'running'. The parent is never read. Children are cancelled only inside roll_up's cancellation branch, and service.cancel touches only the row it is given, so a cancel of the parent does not itself stop any child. Within one tick the ordering is safe (roll_up at orchestration.py:794-795 runs before claim at 805, both under service._lock), but service.cancel does not take service._lock, so a cancel that commits after the roll_up loop and before claim leaves claim promoting a child of an already-cancelled parent. Once promoted, the child stops only at its next durable save (service.save requires state == 'running' and raises CancelledError otherwise), which is after the next capability has already executed.
findings.source: aries/workspace/orchestration.py:718-762 (claim, no parent-state check), aries/workspace/orchestration.py:794-805 (roll_up-then-claim ordering inside tick), aries/workspace/orchestration.py:582-595 (the only place children are cancelled), aries/workspace/service.py:267-277 (cancel updates one row only), aries/workspace/service.py:16 (ACTIVE = {queued, running}), aries/workspace/goal_graph.py:162-172 (dependencies_ready)
findings.reproduction:
DATABASE_URL=sqlite+aiosqlite:////tmp/x.db PYTHONPATH=/home/stamenovmartin/aries/vendor/agentic-core:/home/stamenovmartin/aries/vendor:/home/stamenovmartin/aries /home/stamenovmartin/aries/.venv/bin/python - <<'PY'
import asyncio, json, uuid
from agentic_core.database.base import Base, engine, async_session
from aries.workspace.models import WorkspaceGoal
from aries.workspace.goal_graph import dependencies_ready
async def main():
    async with engine.begin() as c: await c.run_sync(Base.metadata.create_all)
    parent, c1 = uuid.uuid4().hex, uuid.uuid4().hex
    async with async_session() as db:
        db.add(WorkspaceGoal(id=parent, request='p', state='cancelled', result_json=json.dumps({'orchestration':{'role':'parent','dynamic_team':True,'children':[c1]}})))
        db.add(WorkspaceGoal(id=c1, request='Read /tmp/a', state='done', result_json=json.dumps({'final_evidence_refs':['e1'],'orchestration':{'role':'child','parent_id':parent,'depends_on':[]}})))
        await db.commit()
        child = {'orchestration':{'role':'child','parent_id':parent,'depends_on':[c1]}}
        print(await dependencies_ready(db, child))   # -> (True, None) although the parent is cancelled
asyncio.run(main())
PY
findings.why_it_matters: Cancel is the user's hard stop. For an ARIES_GOAL_TEAMS child the grant is read-only and path-exact, so the damage is bounded to unrequested reads after the user said stop. The same claim() also admits the static fan-out path (subgoal kind != 'agent'), where a sub-goal may hold any capability including mutating and desktop ones, so a cancelled parent's queued sub-goal can still touch the machine. The existing test covers only the pre-creation case (tests/test_goal_graph.py:109 test_cancellation_wins_before_graph_creation, which asserts the persist() CAS loses); there is no test for a child admitted after cancellation. The minimal fix is one predicate in claim: re-read the parent row named by orchestration.parent_id and refuse unless it is still 'running'.

findings.title: validate() admits a decomposition whose node order does not match the root requirement order, and synthesize() can then never verify it
findings.observed: EXECUTED PROOF: for goal 'Read <a> and read <b>' (root requirements in order [a, b]), goal_graph.validate ACCEPTED a plan whose nodes were declared [read b, read a]. Feeding the resulting children's steps to agent.completion in the order synthesize() builds them gave met=False ('No current verified evidence satisfies {"capability": "file.read", "path": "<a>"}'), while the same steps in root-requirement order gave met=True. SOURCE INSPECTION: validate's checks are membership-only - 'req not in root_contract[requirements]' and 'any(r not in covered ...)' - so order is never compared. synthesize concatenates children's steps in node declaration order (goal_graph.py:182-187), and completion walks requirements with a strictly increasing cursor over that list (agent.py:58-64), so requirement i must be satisfied by a step after the one that satisfied requirement i-1. A reversed plan therefore fails completion, synthesize appends the rejection to gaps (goal_graph.py:199) and sets the parent to 'partial' (goal_graph.py:209).
findings.source: aries/workspace/goal_graph.py:79-85 (membership-only validation), aries/workspace/goal_graph.py:182-191 (step concatenation in node order), aries/workspace/goal_graph.py:195-209 (completion call and parent state), aries/workspace/agent.py:58-64 (ordered cursor)
findings.reproduction: Script p5 of this review, condensed: compile 'Read /tmp/d/a.txt and read /tmp/d/b.txt'; call goal_graph.validate with nodes [{'id':'n1','goal':'Read /tmp/d/b.txt','capabilities':['file.read']},{'id':'n2','goal':'Read /tmp/d/a.txt','capabilities':['file.read']}] -> accepted; then build two verified file.read steps in that same order with verified file_state evidence and call agent.completion(data, Decision(action='finish', evidence_refs=[both proofs]), ctx) -> (False, 'No current verified evidence satisfies ...'); reverse the two steps -> (True, 'Verified file: ...').
findings.why_it_matters: The model chooses node order, so whether a correct decomposition is reported 'done' or 'partial' is nondeterministic for the same goal. Every child verifiably succeeded and the user is told the goal was only partly achieved. It is also a silent contract break between two modules in the same change: validate declares the plan acceptable and completion declares the same plan unverifiable. Either validate should require the node order to realise the root requirement order (or the dependency edges that imply it), or synthesize should order the concatenated steps by the root contract rather than by node declaration. Both of the author's team tests (tests/test_goal_graph.py:59-60, 112-113) happen to declare nodes in requirement order, so this is invisible to them.

findings.title: Specialist grants come from model-proposed capabilities and the union of all goal paths, not from each node's validated requirements
findings.observed: EXECUTED PROOF: for goal 'Read /tmp/a.txt and read /tmp/b.txt', validate() accepted a node whose only checkable requirement is file.read of /tmp/a.txt but whose capabilities list was all six members of SAFE_READS, and issued it grant caps=['file.exists','file.list','file.read','system.processes','system.status','system.storage'] paths=['/tmp/a.txt','/tmp/b.txt']. Under scopes.use of that grant, scopes.enforce then ALLOWED system.processes {}, system.status {} and file.read {'path': '/tmp/b.txt'} - the sibling's file - and blocked only file.list /tmp and file.read /etc/passwd. Second executed proof: with a root goal whose contract is unsupported ('prepare me a project briefing and read /tmp/a.txt', which goal_graph.eligible() returns True for), validate() accepted a plan of two nodes doing 'List running processes' and 'Check system status', neither of which the user asked for, because the 'req not in root_contract[requirements]' cross-check at goal_graph.py:79 is guarded by root_contract['supported'].
findings.source: aries/workspace/goal_graph.py:21 (SAFE_READS), aries/workspace/goal_graph.py:63-64 (paths = every path matched in the goal text, shared by all nodes), aries/workspace/goal_graph.py:66-82 (grant built from node.capabilities and the goal-wide path set; no check that capabilities are needed by the node's contract), aries/workspace/goal_graph.py:79-80 (root cross-check only when the root contract is supported), aries/workspace/goal_graph.py:95 ('Do not add tasks the user did not ask for' exists only in the prompt), aries/workspace/scopes.py:46-67 (enforce)
findings.reproduction: Script p2 of this review: goal_graph.validate({'nodes':[{'id':'n1','role':'reader','goal':'Read /tmp/a.txt','capabilities':sorted(goal_graph.SAFE_READS),'depends_on':[]},{'id':'n2','role':'reader','goal':'Read /tmp/b.txt','capabilities':['file.read'],'depends_on':[]}]}, 'Read /tmp/a.txt and read /tmp/b.txt', 'ROOT1', expires_at=time.time()+3600) -> accepted; then `with scopes.use(grants['n1']): scopes.enforce(registry.get('system.processes'), {})` -> allowed, and `scopes.enforce(registry.get('file.read'), {'path':'/tmp/b.txt'})` -> allowed. And: goal_graph.validate(plan_of_two_system_probes, 'prepare me a project briefing and read /tmp/a.txt', 'ROOT1', expires_at=...) -> accepted with root_supported=False.
findings.why_it_matters: The module docstring states 'code owns grants'. Code owns the ceiling (SAFE_READS, read_only, exact paths, expiry, no url/session/window) but not the grant: least privilege is delegated to the model, which can hand itself process enumeration, memory/CPU/disk measurement and a sibling's file on a goal that only asked for one read. For a goal whose root contract is unsupported there is no cross-check against the user's request at all, so a benign semantic goal can cause unrequested process and hardware enumeration under the parent's authority, with the only constraint being that each node's own goal happens to be independently checkable. The ceiling is narrow enough that this is a least-privilege defect rather than an escape, and the flag is off by default.

findings.title: verify_probe hardcodes met=True, so the completion recheck for every system.* requirement cannot fail
findings.observed: EXECUTED PROOF: verify_probe(contradictory_executor,'system_probe')({}, {'probes':'ORIGINAL'}, {}) returned {'met': True, 'type': 'system_probe', 'data': {'completely': 'different', 'observed_at': 'now'}} - the verifier reported met although the fresh probe shares nothing with the result it was asked to check. SOURCE INSPECTION: verify_probe re-runs the executor and returns met=True unconditionally; it is the verifier for file.list, file.search, system.status, system.storage, system.processes and task.inspect. completion()'s 'fresh independent check' (agent.py:71-76) therefore reduces, for a system.status / system.storage / system.processes requirement with no 'metric' key, to 'the probe function did not raise'. system.status itself raises only if NO probe is OK (registry.py:303-309). For measurement contracts contracts.measured_readings still gates on the requested metric being present and finite, which is a real check; for the bare 'Check system status' and 'List running processes' contracts there is no content gate at all. Separately, EXECUTED PROOF that contracts.answer for a bare system.status contract returns the literal string 'All supported goal conditions independently verified. See referenced evidence.' - the card for a 'done' status goal contains no status.
findings.source: aries/workspace/registry.py:251-256 (verify_probe), aries/workspace/registry.py:394-405 (its six users), aries/workspace/registry.py:303-309 (status raises only if no probe is OK), aries/workspace/agent.py:71-76 (completion's fresh recheck), aries/workspace/contracts.py:114-118 (evidence_matches returns verification['met'] when the requirement has no metric/url/path/sha), aries/workspace/contracts.py:161-163 (generic answer text)
findings.reproduction: PYTHONPATH=... .venv/bin/python -c "import asyncio; from aries.workspace.registry import verify_probe;\nasync def contradictory(a,c): return {'completely':'different'}\nprint(asyncio.run(verify_probe(contradictory,'system_probe')({}, {'probes':'ORIGINAL'}, {})))" -> met True. And: from aries.workspace import contracts; contracts.answer({'supported':True,'requirements':[{'capability':'system.status'}]}, [{'data':{'probes':[]}}]) -> 'All supported goal conditions independently verified. See referenced evidence.'
findings.why_it_matters: The completion path's whole claim is an independent recheck that can reject a stale or mistaken step. That claim holds strongly for file.read and file.write (proved under 'refuted hypotheses' below) and does not hold for the probe capabilities: the verifier cannot disagree with the executor, so 'independently verified' means 'the probe ran twice'. This is directly relevant to the oo-02 question, because it is the one place in the reviewed completion path where 'done' is decided without any comparison against a requested end state. It is pre-existing rather than introduced by the change under review, but the new automatic finish path (finish_proposal -> completion) now reaches it without a model call. Combined with the generic answer text, a user who asks for the system status gets a green 'done' card that does not contain the status.
findings.status: open, pre-existing, load-bearing for the reviewed path

findings.title: decision.action == 'fail' on an unsupported contract becomes terminal state 'answered', which analytics counts as a success, on model prose alone
findings.observed: SOURCE INSPECTION: in the planner loop, if the first decision is action='fail' with any summary or reason, and there are no steps, and the goal's contract is unsupported, the goal is finished as 'answered' - which sets agent.finished=True and writes a card titled 'Answer' - with zero steps, zero evidence and final_evidence_refs=[]. The gate is only 'contract unsupported', which EXECUTED PROOF confirms covers out-of-scope action requests: contracts.compile_goal('install Visual Studio Code', ...) returns supported=False. aries/analytics/outcomes.py:56 buckets 'answered' as 'succeeded' unconditionally.
findings.source: aries/workspace/agent.py:304-311 (the branch and its in-code justification), aries/workspace/agent.py:220-232 (finish sets finished=True for 'answered'), aries/analytics/outcomes.py:56 (BUCKETS)
findings.reproduction: Source-level: any goal whose contract is unsupported, where agent_planner returns {'action':'fail','summary':'<prose>'} as the first decision and no step has been taken, reaches finish('answered', prose). Confirm the gate with: from aries.workspace import contracts; contracts.compile_goal('install Visual Studio Code', '/tmp')['supported'] -> False. I did NOT execute the planner loop (that needs a model call), so the branch itself is source inspection only.
findings.why_it_matters: This is the shape of the open defect oo-02 reached through the reviewed completion path rather than through a capability: a success-bucketed terminal state with nothing verified and nothing changed, decided by model prose. The in-code comment justifies it for conversational goals ('do you have a student ID?'), which is reasonable, but the condition does not distinguish a conversational goal from an out-of-scope action request. Two mitigations are real and were verified, which is why this is low and not high: the eval harness's reported_success requires a verified step before it will count an 'answered' goal as a claim (eval/agent_suite/checks.py:185-188), and traces._plan_of drops rows with no verified step so these never become few-shot 'worked before' examples (aries/workspace/traces.py:118-120). The exposure is the product's own success-rate metric, which is exactly the number a thesis would quote.
findings.status: open by design; the analytics bucketing is the part that is probably unintended

findings.title: verify_exists reports met=True for a file that does not exist, which relabels a wholly failed read goal as 'partial'
findings.observed: EXECUTED PROOF (with aries.workspace.capabilities.checked_path stubbed to an identity function, because the real one needs settings this harness does not create): verify_exists({'path': '<missing>'}, executor_result, ctx) returned {'met': True, 'type': 'file_state', 'data': {'path': '<missing>', 'exists': False, 'is_file': False, ...}}. SOURCE INSPECTION: met is 'fresh[exists] == result.get(exists)', i.e. it verifies that the observation was accurate, not that any goal condition holds. agent.py then picks the terminal state with "'partial' if any(e['verified'] for e in data['evidence']) else 'failed'" at both the terminal-read-failure exit and the budget-exhausted exits.
findings.source: aries/workspace/registry.py:187-189 (verify_exists), aries/workspace/agent.py:431 (terminal-read-failure exit), aries/workspace/agent.py:297-302 and 433-434 (the other exits using the same predicate)
findings.reproduction: PYTHONPATH=... .venv/bin/python with capabilities.checked_path monkeypatched to `async def stub(db, raw, *, write=False): return pathlib.Path(raw)`, then `await verify_exists({'path':'/tmp/definitely-absent'}, await exists({'path':'/tmp/definitely-absent'}, {'db':db}), {'db':db})` -> met True.
findings.why_it_matters: A goal 'Read /missing.txt' in which the planner first calls file.exists and then file.read ends as 'partial' rather than 'failed', because the non-existence was recorded as verified evidence. It cannot reach 'done' (no contract in contracts.compile_goal ever produces a file.exists requirement, so it can never satisfy one), so this is a state-labelling and analytics-bucketing defect rather than a false success. The capability description already steers the planner away from this route ('For read goals use file.read directly') but nothing enforces it.

findings.title: goal_graph.persist mutates the caller's data dict before its CAS and does not restore it when the CAS loses
findings.observed: SOURCE INSPECTION ONLY. persist writes data['orchestration'] = {'role':'parent','dynamic_team':True,'children':[...], ...} and data['steps'] = [] before issuing the conditional UPDATE. If rowcount != 1 the database is rolled back (so no children are created) and False is returned, but the in-memory data keeps the parent-role orchestration block naming children that do not exist. agent.run then falls through to _run with that dict, which creates a fresh agent block and persists the whole dict, so the durable row now advertises role='parent' with non-existent child IDs. orchestration.tick then treats the row as a parent on every pass and roll_up returns None forever at the 'len(rows) != len(children)' guard, while the ordinary dispatcher's orphan sweep deliberately skips role=='parent' rows.
findings.source: aries/workspace/goal_graph.py:151-157 (mutation before the CAS, rollback without restore), aries/workspace/agent.py:111-118 (fall-through to _run on False), aries/workspace/orchestration.py:596 (roll_up's len guard), aries/workspace/service.py:754 (orphan sweep skips parents)
findings.reproduction: Not reproduced: the CAS can only lose if another writer changes the row between the db.get and the UPDATE in the same function (the state != 'running' case is caught earlier at goal_graph.py:139), and I did not want to drive concurrent writers against a live queue. Read the two statements at goal_graph.py:151-157 against the early return at 139 to see that no snapshot of data is taken and nothing restores it.
findings.why_it_matters: A lost race leaves a self-inconsistent durable row whose orchestration block describes a team that was never created. Because the row then claims to be a parent, it is exempt from the interrupted-goal sweep and only its own execution finishing saves it. The fix is one line: deep-copy or snapshot data before mutating, and restore on the rollback path.

findings.title: synthesize discards the verified root answer and always uses 'done', never 'answered'
findings.observed: SOURCE INSPECTION ONLY. synthesize calls completion and uses its summary only on the failure path (gaps.append(summary)). On the success path only final_evidence_refs is kept; data['cards'] is rebuilt purely from per-child observations, so the root answer that contracts.answer composed - the file contents for a compound read, 'Highest observed filesystem usage: ...' for a disk goal, the spoken measurement sentence for a measurement goal - never reaches the user. The same line sets parent.state = 'done' unconditionally, whereas the single-goal path sets 'answered' when contract['answer'] == 'measurements'.
findings.source: aries/workspace/goal_graph.py:195-199 (summary used only when not verified), aries/workspace/goal_graph.py:204-205 (cards rebuilt from child observations), aries/workspace/goal_graph.py:209 (state always 'done' when verified), aries/workspace/agent.py:322 (the single-goal path's 'answered' for measurement contracts)
findings.reproduction: Read goal_graph.py:195-209. The variable `summary` returned by completion is referenced exactly once, at line 199, inside `else: gaps.append(summary)`.
findings.why_it_matters: The voice reply layer and the UI are keyed on goal state and cards (aries/speech/replies.py:241 branches on state; contracts.answer calls that same sentence builder for measurement contracts). A measurement or disk goal routed through a team therefore lands in a different state than the same goal routed directly, and the sentence that IS the answer is computed, used as a liveness check, and thrown away. For compound reads the children's own summaries happen to cover most of the content, which is why this is low rather than moderate.

findings.title: completion_progress.reject can spend the single correction allowance on the code-generated automatic proposal
findings.observed: SOURCE INSPECTION ONLY. finish_proposal.propose can emit a finish Decision with no model call; agent.py records it as a decision and runs it through the same completion check. If completion rejects it, reject() records count=1 against the current step_count. Because propose() then refuses to fire again at the same step count, the planner is called; if the model's own first response is also 'finish' at that same step count, that is the second rejection and the goal stops with stop_reason COMPLETION_NO_PROGRESS. completion_progress.py's docstring describes the budget as 'Allow one corrected proposal', which the automatic proposer can consume before the model ever claims anything.
findings.source: aries/workspace/agent.py:244-252 (automatic proposal recorded and checked), aries/workspace/agent.py:329-334 (reject call site), aries/workspace/completion_progress.py:12-26, aries/workspace/finish_proposal.py:13 (automatic_finish_step_count suppresses a repeat at the same step count)
findings.reproduction: Read the three call sites together. Not executed: driving the loop needs a planner response, i.e. a model call.
findings.why_it_matters: It fails in the safe direction - it stops rather than claiming success - and the rejection also demotes the matching step to 'stale' with a retryable hint, so the correct next move really is an action rather than another finish claim. Reported because the docstring's stated allowance and the actual allowance differ, which matters if this guard is ever cited as a measured property.

refuted_hypotheses.title: The terminal-failure shortcut can fire on a goal that still had achievable requirements
refuted_hypotheses.checked: EXECUTED PROOF of terminal_failure.reason over eight variants of a synthetic failed step: genuine single missing read -> returns the message; two-requirement contract -> None; step path differs from the requested path -> None; retryable=True -> None; code='TRANSIENT' -> None; error_type='OSError' -> None; contract supported=False -> None; observation evidence whose data does not equal the step's error -> None. Also checked by source and by executed contract compilation that contracts.compile_goal cannot produce a one-requirement file.read contract without a path (the only such branch is the anchored 'Read <path>' fullmatch) and cannot produce a one-requirement compound contract (the compound branch requires 2..4 clauses, each contributing at least one requirement), so 'exactly one file.read requirement' really does mean 'the entire user goal was this one read'. Checked the error provenance too: sources.safety.check_path raises SourceRejected with its own codes (PATH_EXCLUDED, PROTECTED_PATH), never FileNotFoundError; registry.file_snapshot uses open_nofollow, so a symlink yields ELOOP/OSError rather than FileNotFoundError; agent.error only assigns TARGET_NOT_FOUND to an actual FileNotFoundError.
refuted_hypotheses.verdict: REFUTED. The shortcut is scoped as its author claims: a single supported file.read requirement, exact requested path (compared after Path.expanduser().absolute(), so '/tmp/./nope.txt' matches '/tmp/nope.txt' - the same file, still exact), a genuine non-retryable FileNotFoundError/TARGET_NOT_FOUND, and a matching persisted execution_error evidence row with verified=False whose data equals the step error. I found no input that makes it fire while achievable work remained. The one residual nit is CR-06: when it does fire, the partial-vs-failed label can be wrong.

refuted_hypotheses.title: completion() accepts evidence_refs that were not produced by verified steps
refuted_hypotheses.checked: EXECUTED PROOF against a real file on an isolated database: invented random ref -> (False, 'Finish requires existing verified evidence IDs; unknown/failed references rejected'); the step's unverified execution_observation ref -> same rejection; empty refs -> same rejection; a genuine verified ref whose step's verification_status was set to 'verification_failed' -> (False, 'No current verified evidence satisfies ...'). Source-checked that step['evidence_refs'] is only ever appended the verifier's proof id (agent.py:392-393), that refs must be a subset of the verified-evidence set (agent.py:54-57), and that selection additionally requires a non-empty intersection with that specific step's own refs (agent.py:64) - so a ref belonging to one step can never authorise another.
refuted_hypotheses.verdict: REFUTED. Evidence cannot be forged or borrowed across steps through the finish decision.

refuted_hypotheses.title: completion() accepts stale evidence from an earlier step that no longer holds
refuted_hypotheses.checked: EXECUTED PROOF: an honest finish on an unchanged file returned (True, 'Verified file: ... original'); rewriting the file behind ARIES's back and replaying the identical finish returned (False, 'No current verified evidence satisfies ...') and demoted the step to verification_status='stale'; deleting the file returned the same rejection. Source-checked that the recheck is a real re-observation for the file capabilities (registry.verify_read re-reads and compares sha256 and path; registry.verify_write re-reads and compares against the requested content hash) and that contracts.evidence_matches additionally pins path, sha256, url and metric where the requirement carries them.
refuted_hypotheses.verdict: REFUTED for file.read and file.write, which are the capabilities every file contract depends on - with the explicit caveat recorded as CR-04: the guarantee is exactly as strong as the capability's verifier, and for the six verify_probe capabilities the recheck cannot fail.

refuted_hypotheses.title: A goal-graph child can widen its grant, outlive its parent's authority, or hold a write capability
refuted_hypotheses.checked: EXECUTED PROOF: nesting scopes.use of a wider grant inside a narrower one -> PermissionError 'A specialist cannot widen inherited authority'; a grant whose expires_at is in the past -> scopes.enforce raises PermissionError 'Specialist grant expired'; a node asking for file.write -> validate raises PermissionError 'Specialist capability is outside the bounded read surface'; a node naming /etc/passwd when the goal did not -> PermissionError 'Model introduced a path the user did not name'; a node doing unrelated work when the root contract IS supported -> PermissionError 'Model introduced an unrelated root requirement'; a decomposition that drops one of the root's requested conditions -> ValueError 'Decomposition omitted a requested condition'; a self-dependency -> 'Dependency cycle'; an unknown dependency id -> 'Unknown dependency'. Source-checked that Grant is frozen with extra='forbid', that validate_registry refuses any non-read or approval-requiring capability under read_only, and that enforce rejects url/session/window_id arguments outright and resolves paths at use time to catch a changed symlink.
refuted_hypotheses.verdict: REFUTED. The grant ceiling holds. What does not hold is least privilege inside that ceiling, which is CR-03.

refuted_hypotheses.title: A child escapes or resets the root resource budget
refuted_hypotheses.checked: SOURCE INSPECTION: agent.run derives root_id from orchestration.parent_id and only then calls budgets.create(root_id, ...), which issues an INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING on root_id. A child therefore attaches to the parent's existing budget row rather than resetting its counters or extending its deadline, and every capability and verification call reserves against that same root (agent._budgeted_capability -> budgets.reserve with attribution['root_id']). The author's own test asserts the arithmetic (tests/test_goal_graph.py:97-98 checks the root's tool count across parent and children).

refuted_hypotheses.title: A zero-evidence 'answered' goal poisons later planning as a 'worked before' example, or lets a team parent reach 'done'
refuted_hypotheses.checked: SOURCE INSPECTION: traces._plan_of keeps only steps whose verification.met is True and traces.successes drops any candidate row whose plan is empty, so a zero-step 'answered' row is never offered to the planner. For the team path, goal_graph.validate requires every node's own contract to be supported, while the fail->answered branch requires the contract to be UNsupported, so that branch is unreachable for a team child; and goal_graph.dependencies_ready additionally requires a non-empty final_evidence_refs before a dependent child may run.
refuted_hypotheses.verdict: REFUTED on both counts. The residual exposure is only the analytics bucketing, recorded as CR-05.

refuted_hypotheses.title: A 'held' child leaves its parent running forever
refuted_hypotheses.checked: SOURCE INSPECTION plus EXECUTED PROOF that service.ACTIVE == {'running','queued'}. Because 'held' is not ACTIVE, roll_up's wait guard passes and synthesize runs; a held child's state is not in {'done','answered'} so it becomes a gap and the parent is reported 'partial'. Also executed-proved that dependencies_ready correctly returns (False, reason) for a prerequisite that is 'done' but carries no final_evidence_refs, and (False, None) - skip, do not hold - for a prerequisite still running.
refuted_hypotheses.verdict: REFUTED; the parent does roll up honestly. Noted as a side observation, not a finding: a 'held' child is never re-queued by claim (which selects only state == 'queued') and is not cancelled by roll_up's cancellation pass (which covers ACTIVE | {'proposed'}), so it stays 'held' as an inert row forever.

refuted_hypotheses.title: A goal can be expanded twice, or expansion can destroy work the parent had already done
refuted_hypotheses.checked: SOURCE INSPECTION: agent.run guards expansion on 'not data.get(execution_scope) and not data.get(graph_considered)' and sets graph_considered before calling expand, and expand persists that flag on both its failure paths. Expansion happens before _run, so data['steps'] is necessarily empty when persist clears it. persist is a single transaction: children are db.add-ed and the parent's UPDATE is conditioned on state == 'running' AND result_json == the exact value read, so a concurrent cancel loses nothing and creates no orphans (the author's test tests/test_goal_graph.py:109-121 asserts exactly this).
refuted_hypotheses.verdict: REFUTED, except for the in-memory residue when the CAS loses, recorded as CR-07.

refuted_hypotheses.title: A team parent is left running forever because nothing supervises it after agent.run returns early
refuted_hypotheses.checked: SOURCE INSPECTION: service._execute's m14 branch awaits agent.run and returns without writing a terminal state, service.execute only records routing telemetry for states in {done, partial, failed}, and _supervise's except branches fire only on an exception. orchestration.tick heartbeats every running/cancelled parent on each pass and the ordinary dispatcher's orphan sweep deliberately skips role == 'parent', so the parent survives until roll_up.
refuted_hypotheses.verdict: REFUTED. One residual observation, not a finding: while runtime maintenance is active, tick returns before the heartbeat loop, so a parent is neither heartbeated nor swept - which is the safe direction (it is not falsely marked interrupted).
